title: 🎁 Wrapped in Blue
content:

Why wear a dress when you can wear the bow?

title: Graphic flattens texture and causes render issues
content:
Hi!  
I’m trying to render a **sublimation print on a t-shirt** in CLO (v2025.0.400 – Mac), but I can’t get it to work properly.

  * If I apply a full-size graphic in 2D with **Z-Offset = 0** , I get **mesh triangulation/glitches** in the render.

  * If I increase the Z-Offset (e.g. 0.1 mm), the glitches disappear — but the **puckering, fabric texture, and seams between panels** become invisible or flattened.

  * I’ve tried different formats (PDF, JPG, PNG), turned off “Use Same Map as Fabric”, removed all normal/displacement/opacity maps, cleared cache… still stuck.




I’d like the print to:

  * follow the **puckering and folds**

  * **preserve the fabric’s normal and texture details**

  * and render cleanly, without artifacts.




Is there any known fix or recommended workaround?

Also, I’m often unable to input decimal values correctly in CLO (Mac). For example, when I try to type **0.1** , CLO automatically switches it to **1.0** — not just in Z-Offset, but in other fields too. I can’t tell if this is a locale/keyboard issue or a bug.

Thanks so much!  
Nicole

![f87e5b315a234d0d8446076e98431650](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202507/376eb8c5482c433e95d3c092b8273652/images/f87e5b315a234d0d8446076e98431650Screenshot%202025-07-19%20at%2001.04.09.png)![c861f5f1ecb54a17a124361ebe867f3d](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202507/376eb8c5482c433e95d3c092b8273652/images/c861f5f1ecb54a17a124361ebe867f3dScreenshot%202025-07-19%20at%2001.04.48.png)![ff7bbd5e6f804e89ac6aeaed5e25814c](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202507/376eb8c5482c433e95d3c092b8273652/images/ff7bbd5e6f804e89ac6aeaed5e25814cScreenshot%202025-07-19%20at%2001.02.05.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi Nicole, the offset being on 0 is an occurrence that cannot be avoided, in the case of your graphic placement I have another suggestion that will keep everything intact as you wish for. Copy your fabric, assign it to the sleeve, apply the graphic as a base color map, then edit the placement of the sleeve on the fabric roll in the Print Layout. About the decimal issue, it is a bug in the patch you are on (400). Update to the latest patch 408 and decimals are working fine again.
Reply 1: Hi Melody, thank you so much for your reply!I understand your suggestion and I’ll definitely try it out.However, I was wondering: what if I wanted to keep using the graphic application method instead of mapping the print into the fabric texture?I find the graphic tool very useful because it allows me to precisely place the artwork where the invisible seam margins are (the folded or stitched parts, not visible unless baselines are active). This helps me see the actual positioning inside the full pattern piece, including all the seam allowances, and easily spot mistakes in the artwork placement — which wouldn’t be as clear when working with a trimmed version of the shape.I’m still a CLO newbie and learning a lot every day, so maybe I’m missing something! :)Thanks again!
Reply 2: Hi Nicole, I am not sure I understand fully, but if using graphics is the preferable workflow for you to reach a good visualization, then nothing speaks against it!
Reply 3: Hi Melody,Thank you again! I’d like to clarify that my concern is not about workflow preference, but a technical limitation I’m facing.When I apply a full graphic using the Graphic Tool and set the Offset to 0 (which is necessary for correct placement in my case), CLO completely flattens the fabric’s texture, removing visible normal maps, puckering, and seam details – this is the core of my issue.I’m trying to achieve a realistic sublimation print simulation, where the artwork is visible on top of the fabric but doesn’t erase the material’s physical properties.I know I could embed the print into the base color map, but this doesn’t give me the same control – I specifically need to see the full pattern shape with seam allowances visible (which the Graphic Tool lets me do). It’s essential for me to verify placement accuracy.So my question is:Is there any way to preserve fabric details (like normals and puckering) while using the Graphic Tool with Offset = 0?I’d really appreciate any technical insight – I’m still new to CLO and trying to understand its limits. Thanks again!
Reply 4: Hi Nicole, the Graphic Offset on 0 will always collide with the pattern piece's mesh and create a flecked effect, unfortunately, there is no way around. "I specifically need to see the full pattern shape with seam allowances visible (which the Graphic Tool lets me do). It’s essential for me to verify placement accuracy." Sorry, I am still confused. All of this is visible in the Print Layout - the pattern piece can be dragged and dropped onto the desired position with seam allowance visible. Let me know what I'm still not getting, maybe with a screenshot? Thank you :)
content_description: This page seeks solutions and advice for accurately rendering sublimation prints on t-shirts in CLO 2025 for Mac, addressing mesh glitches, fabric detail preservation, and decimal input issues.

title: 👑 Denim Royalty
content:
There's something magical about turning a traditionally casual fabric into something majestic. With _Denim Royalty_ , I wanted to explore how far denim could go when treated like couture — structured, voluminous, and with a bit of drama.

This look features a corseted upper silhouette that hugs the torso, balanced by two exaggerated puff sleeves that bring immediate visual impact. The sleeves are constructed with layered pattern pieces and volume modifiers to create a soft yet sculptural shape, mimicking the petals of a blooming flower — only in denim.

The lower part flows into a siren skirt with a soft flare and a distressed edge finish. I intentionally kept the seams exposed and slightly frayed to contrast the gown-like structure with a sense of rawness and deconstruction. It’s a clash between elegance and edge — and I love that tension.

Let me know — would you wear couture denim to a gala? Because I definitely would 💙

title: CONNECT upload issues, which file formats are supported by thumbnails when the store uploads files？
content:
CONNECT upload issues, what file formats does the thumbnail support when the store uploads a file?  
I flipped through the reference manual:  
Supported image formats: jpeg/.png/.bmp, supported video formats: webp, videos in non-WEBP formats such as MP4, AVI, etc. must be converted to WEBP format and uploaded as thumbnails.  
Why can't I upload thumbnails when I convert video format to WEBP format?  
Can I only upload jpeg/.png/.bmp?  
Can I upload only attached images in WEBP format?  
The last time I uploaded the attached image to the file, I added an image in WEBP format, but the attached image could not be seen after the upload was successful.  
I now have a question about whether thumbnails can be used above transmission diagrams, and what formats are supported?![984edb8db639462aa74cdc203a3dca82](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202507/9eae1e2cde2d45c29f690f5a7ff0545e/images/984edb8db639462aa74cdc203a3dca82675aef31082482f3e6134c70dadec81e.png)![adf14aacb52e4a1a8391e6eb99985ad0](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202507/9eae1e2cde2d45c29f690f5a7ff0545e/images/adf14aacb52e4a1a8391e6eb99985ad0dde18e76b9db50daf0ba04dd6056d177.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi, CLO footageWe limit thumbnail uploads to JPG and PNG only, in order to ensure a seamless browsing experience for users when viewing items. Since loading speed is less critical when opening an item's detail page, WebP animation can be used for additional images.When using WebP animation, it is limited to a total of 50 megapixels (the sum of sizes of all frames). This is a guideline of the image delivery service used on our platform. If this limit is exceeded, the WebP image may not be displayed properly.
Reply 1: Okay, thanks for the answer, the reference manual can explain it properly or mark the thumbnail with JPG and PNG upload only
